text.p: FIFA has threatened Deportivo Coruna with disciplinary action unless the club halts a civil court action against the Spanish Football Federation.

FIFA intervened at the request of the federation after Deportivo won an appeal against a one-game home ban in the Spanish courts. The incident which sparked the showdown occurred when a referee was hit by a coin during a league match in Coruna.
The federation banned the club from playing their next game at home -- a sell-out cup clash with Barcelona.

Deportivo went to court and gained an injunction allowing them to play the match. The injunction remained in place afterwards, enabling the club to keep clear of the suspension -- and incurring FIFA's wrath.
FIFA's disciplinary committee meet on February 19 and if the situation is not resolved will take action.

"FIFA has told the Spanish F.A. that Deportivo must stop its legal action," said world soccer governing body spokesman Keith Cooper. "It must accept the Spanish F.A. constitution the same way the Spanish F.A. accepts FIFA's.
"Football must run its own legal affairs and keep them out of the public courts or the whole structure of the sport will collapse.
"We cannot have teams running in and out of courts protesting over decisions or no game would ever get played."

Spanish newspapers said Deportivo had withdrawn its legal action last week but Cooper said the correct procedures had not been followed and that a poroper withdrawal would have to be made for the Spanish club to avoid punishment.
He said the increasing number of cases going before civil courts has overwhelmed FIFA and left it considering a total news blackout in cases facing litigation.
"It (a news blackout) is something we are considering," said Cooper. "In this increasingly complicated legal landscape we cannot handle all the cases that are pending.
"It is impossible to keep people up to date.
"Some feel that by having their cases in the news they are being prejudiced by media exposure.
"We know we're not dealing with murder cases but nonetheless we have to try and be fair to all parties."
